privacy.description: What LEAF-Writer stores locally and what it only sends if you choose to use a networked feature.
privacy.summary: LEAF-Writer is mostly local-first in normal desktop use. Your files, databases, and settings stay on your machine unless you use a feature that explicitly talks to another service.
privacy.local_first: Normal editing, local entity databases, offline packs, and most settings remain on your computer.
privacy.documents_body: The user name you enter in Settings can be written into your documents as project/document metadata. That name travels with the file because it becomes part of the document itself, not because the app uploads it somewhere automatically.
privacy.leaderboard_body: If you choose to submit your service record to the leaderboard, LEAF-Writer sends your GitHub identity token for verification, your displayed user name/rank context, your achievement metrics counts, and your optional avatar image to the leaderboard service.
privacy.telemetry_body: The editor code supports optional Sentry crash/error reporting if a build enables it. That is configuration-dependent rather than a normal editing requirement.
privacy.web_body: In the web app, anonymous Google Analytics page/editor events can be sent only if measurement cookies are accepted. The desktop app does not use that cookie-consent analytics flow.
